drafts.title: Front seats provide extended thigh support and long-lasting cushion comfort for tall drivers
drafts.description: Tall drivers experience noticeably improved thigh support and sustained seat comfort over time: the front seat cushion offers a user-adjustable thigh extension and cushion construction that keeps comfort and support after prolonged use.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion must offer an adjustable thigh extension range of at least 80 mm and, after a simulated 1000-cycle durability test, cushion thickness loss shall be ≤10% and subjective comfort score (user panel, n=30) remains ≥4/5.
assumptions: An 80 mm adjustment range meaningfully improves thigh support for drivers up to ~195 cm tall based on current BMW anthropometric targets.
Simulated 1000-cycle test approximates ~3 years of typical use.
Seat foam formulation achieving <10% thickness loss is feasible within 3–5 year successor timeline.
uncertainties: Exact ergonomic benefit for the tallest percentile (>195 cm) may vary by body shape.
Durability test correlation to real-world feel and long-term perceived comfort may vary.

drafts.title: Seat memory reliably restores saved positions every time
drafts.description: When a driver recalls a saved seat position the vehicle restores the seat to the saved geometry consistently and within a tight tolerance so drivers do not need to manually re-adjust.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Seat memory shall restore the saved position within ±20 mm linear and ±3° angular accuracy in at least 95% of 50 consecutive recall cycles during validation testing.
assumptions: Tolerance band ±20 mm / ±3° is perceived by customers as 'accurate' restoration.
Testing covers typical cabin temperature ranges and electrical states.
uncertainties: Software/hardware interactions (e.g., seat calibration drift) may produce edge cases outside tolerance that need specific root-cause fixes.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with a wide palette and multiple brightness levels per zone
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior ambient lighting with many colors and fine-grained brightness control across multiple zones so lighting feels premium and flexible.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting offers at least 64 distinct selectable colors and at least 8 discrete brightness levels, with independent control of at least 3 cabin zones, validated in the user interface and in cabin appearance tests.
assumptions: 64 colors and 8 brightness levels provide a perceptibly larger choice set than the current vehicle.
3 zones (driver, passenger, rear) cover primary personalization needs for this segment.
uncertainties: Later regulatory constraints on interior illumination or distracted-driving concerns may limit some modes.

drafts.title: Everyday practicality: cup holders fit common bottles and trunk offers a powered socket for portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers can place common bottles and travel mugs securely in cup holders, and they can power a portable cooler from the trunk without needing adapters.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept bottles/mugs up to 85 mm diameter and secure them against lateral acceleration up to 0.8 g; trunk includes a permanently installed 12 V socket rated for at least 10 A (120 W) accessible to common cooler plugs.
assumptions: 85 mm diameter covers the majority of common bottles and travel mugs in the target market.
A 10 A/120 W trunk socket is sufficient for typical 12 V cooler boxes customers intend to use.
uncertainties: Some large-format bottles or non-standard cooler plugs may still not be compatible.
Packaging constraints in higher-trim variants may require different socket placement.

drafts.title: Hands‑free tailgate operates reliably on first attempt
drafts.description: The hands-free tailgate opens consistently when the customer performs the required gesture, minimizing repeated attempts and frustration.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free tailgate opens successfully on the first valid gesture in ≥95% of 100 real-world gesture attempts across common footwear, carry conditions and lighting, with mean open time ≤2.0 s after gesture completion.
assumptions: 95% first-attempt success is a user-meaningful reliability target.
Testing scenarios include obstructed foot trajectories and common loading states (empty/loaded).
uncertainties: Extreme dirt/icing conditions or unusual footwear may still reduce success rates; fallbacks should be defined.

drafts.title: Rear legroom at least matches main rivals in the segment
drafts.description: Rear-seat passengers enjoy legroom that is equal to or better than the segment's main competitors so the 5 Series remains competitive for rear occupant comfort.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured rear knee clearance (rear knee point to front seat back) must be ≥980 mm in the baseline seating configuration and, in internal benchmark tests, must be no worse than the top two segment competitors at launch.
assumptions: A 980 mm knee clearance target is realistic for matching/exceeding competitors in the D/E executive segment at successor launch.
Benchmark comparisons use standardized measurement methodology aligned with rival published specs.
uncertainties: Platform dimensional constraints may force trade-offs with trunk volume or exterior proportions.
Competitor published figures may change by successor launch; adaptive benchmarking will be needed.

drafts.title: Flush door handles operate in freezing conditions and with light ice build-up
drafts.description: Owners can open doors reliably in winter: flush door handles must function despite low temperatures and common ice accumulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Handles must reliably open in environmental chamber tests down to -30 °C and after an ice layer up to 5 mm thickness, demonstrated across 50 repeated cycles without failure.
assumptions: Performance to -30 °C and 5 mm ice covers the vast majority of cold-climate use cases in target markets.
Validation testing simulates real-world stuck/ice scenarios customers encounter.
uncertainties: Severe glaze ice or road salt accumulation may still require de-icing procedures beyond mechanical design.

drafts.title: Requested specific component: 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked for the volume knob to use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder (engineering-level request). This draft records the explicit component ask but is out of scope for product-facing requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specifies a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder per customer request (component-level).
drafts.scope_reason: This is a request for a specific component/part (engineering specification) rather than a customer-facing outcome; engineering should handle feasibility and selection.

drafts.title: Customer outcome tied to volume knob request: physical volume control feels precise and never misses inputs
drafts.description: Drivers can adjust audio volume with the physical knob precisely and without missed steps or jumps while driving, delivering predictable tactile control.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Physical volume knob allows at least 32 distinct incremental steps perceived by users and registers every step in 100% of 100 test rotations under typical driving vibration and temperature conditions.
assumptions: Delivering 32 perceptible, reliably registered steps satisfies customers' desire for precise tactile control.
Achieving 100% registration in test conditions is feasible with appropriate encoder and signal processing.
uncertainties: Exact implementation (encoder type, signal filtering) is an engineering choice; satisfaction depends on tactile detents and software response.

drafts.title: Requested specific component: side windows made from 4.5 mm laminated glass (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked explicitly for 4.5 mm laminated side glass. This draft records the explicit material/thickness ask but is an engineering-level specification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specifies 4.5 mm laminated side glass per customer request (component-level).
drafts.scope_reason: Specific glass thickness is an engineering material specification; the customer-facing outcome (improved acoustic/quality perception) is handled separately if desired.

drafts.title: Customer-facing acoustic/quality outcome tied to side glass request: reduced cabin noise and perceived solidity
drafts.description: Passengers perceive lower external noise and a more solid cabin when windows are closed, improving perceived quality.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: With side windows closed, exterior-to-cabin broadband noise at 100 km/h is reduced by at least 2 dB(A) compared to the current model baseline in standardized driving noise tests.
assumptions: Using thicker/laminated glass is a primary feasible measure to reduce cabin noise by ~2 dB(A) at highway speeds.
Baseline measurements of the current model are available for direct comparison.
uncertainties: Actual noise reduction depends on glazing, sealing, and other NVH measures; glass alone may not achieve full 2 dB(A) without additional measures.

drafts.title: Requested specific component: seat cushion foam density 55 kg/m³ (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers requested seat foam density of 55 kg/m³. This draft logs the specific material density request but is an engineering-level specification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specifies seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ per customer request (component-level).
drafts.scope_reason: Specific foam density is an engineering/materials specification; the customer-facing seat comfort requirement is captured in a separate draft.

drafts.title: Pedestrian protection and front-end design complies with applicable regional pedestrian protection regulations (record of customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the front end meets the new EU pedestrian protection regulation; regulatory compliance and homologation items are recorded here for engineering/regulatory teams.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Design must meet the applicable pedestrian protection regulation(s) in each market per regulatory certification testing.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a regulation/homologation requirement; out of scope for customer-facing product requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag certification per FMVSS 208 requested (record of customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers ask that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification; certification and homologation tasks should be handled by regulatory/engineering teams.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Airbag system obtains FMVSS 208 certification for rear seats as required by the market.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a regulation/certification request (FMVSS 208); out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern to follow ECE R112 where applicable (record of customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers requested headlights that follow the ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market; record for engineering/homologation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Headlamp beam pattern meets ECE R112 requirements where applicable and is certified for each launch market requiring it.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific regulatory beam pattern compliance is a homologation requirement and out of scope for customer-facing feature drafting.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (business ask)
drafts.description: Customers requested that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years. This is a commercial/financial request to be addressed by the business team.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Business to evaluate and respond to request for a 60% residual value guarantee after five years.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a business/financial request (residual value guarantee), not a vehicle-level customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Production cost reduction request (business ask)
drafts.description: Customers/users asked that BMW cut production cost per car by 8%. This is an internal business/operations request for the company to consider.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Business/operations to evaluate feasibility of an 8% production cost reduction per car.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a corporate cost/production target request and out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.
